# Implement block: Clay Press Blob (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Clay Press Blob" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A blob of satin modelling clay sits on a seamless paper sweep tinted with its own colour, like a tonal product shot: terracotta on peach paper, cobalt on pale blue. It is lit from the upper left, with a soft sheen that rides the shape, a darker rim toward the lower right, a fine grain, and contact shadows in the paper's deep tone. It is a soft body that keeps what you do to it for a while: a press sinks a dent with a fingerprint in it (pressed near the edge, it notches the rim), a drag pulls out a lump, a flick throws it against the side of the stage where it squashes into a rounded slab and wobbles back, and a pinch squeezes it. A tap recolours the clay, the new colour spreading from the finger while the paper and the ink turn with it. "Clay Study" and "Nº 04" sit above the clay's name in a large bold serif, and "Press · Pull · Flick · Pinch · Tap to recolour" below.

**Motion.** The clay is a ring of 48 mass points around the centroid, stepped in fixed 1/240 s substeps (a frame counts for at most 1/30 s). Each point is pulled to its place on a rest shape (130 /s², 420 /s² while pinched), tied to its neighbours by edge springs (2600 /s², damping 6) and a bending stiffness (900 /s²), and pushed out by the trapped area (26000 pt/s² per unit of area lost), so a dent in one place bulges the clay elsewhere. Wobble damps at 3.4 /s, the whole body at 0.6 /s, and a home spring (11 /s², 4.6 /s) brings it back to the middle. The rest shape is plastic: a point pushed more than 3 pt off it drags it along at 5.5 /s, and the marks creep back round at 0.95 /s while smoothing along the ring at 2.2 /s. The radius is the smallest of 30% of the width, 30% of the stage height and 132 pt. Press: from touch-down the finger sinks a dent (30 pt across at full depth, growing at 6.5 /s) and widens the clay by up to 7 pt toward its side; a dent within reach of the rim draws the rim points it overlaps in toward the centre (up to 11 pt, 260 /s², a Gaussian along the rim), so a press at the edge notches the edge; a finger that lands outside the clay pushes the rim in as a 24 pt disc on a soft contact spring (2600 /s², damping 30). The dent holds 0.9 s after the lift and fills back in over 2.6 s, its six fingerprint loops fading in 1.5 s. Drag: after 9 pt the finger takes hold of the rim within 46 pt (or, from inside, the side it pulls toward), a Gaussian patch 2.4 points wide on a 950 /s² spring, rubber-banded so the lump never passes 130 pt and eased (tanh) to stay 26 pt inside the walls; let go and it springs back with a wobble. Faster than 700 pt/s the release throws the body as one piece (each point keeps 10% of its own motion) at 45% of the finger's speed, at most 850 pt/s. The stage's walls (20 pt in from the sides, under the header and above the hint) are soft: a point meets a spring 28 pt before a wall that grows from nothing across that cushion and stiffens past the wall (2200 /s² × (1 + (depth/12)²), damping 40, a light grip of 4 /s along it), so the clay slows, squashes into a rounded slab and rebounds, with a medium haptic; nothing stops dead on a line. Pinch: the shape stretches by the ratio of the fingers' spans along their axis (0.6–1.5, a quarter beyond) and by its inverse square root across; on release 30% of the squeeze stays. A tap shorter than 0.26 s cycles six clays: the new colour spreads from the finger as a soft-edged disc over 0.75 s on an ease-in-out curve, mixed in RGB (no detour through other hues); the paper (the clay's hue at 34/40/30% of its saturation and lightness 0.86/0.91/0.80, top to floor), the shadows and the ink (lightness 0.24) turn with it over the same 0.75 s, and the name crossfades (out over 180 ms, in over 300 ms after 120 ms). The sheen is satin: a broad glow at 22% and a soft hot spot at 60%. Haptics: soft when a press starts a dent, a selection tick on recolour, light when a pull or pinch lets go. The self-playing demo pokes at 0.6 and 1.7 s, presses the right rim at 2.7 s, pulls the upper right out and lets go at 4 s, taps to cobalt at 5.8 s, flicks the clay into the right wall at 7 s, pinches it at 9.2 s, taps back to terracotta at 11 s and repeats every 14 s (LOOP); a touch pauses it for 3 s. Under reduced motion the demo does not play, a flick throws nothing, the wobble damps three times faster and the colour crossfades. A non-finite state lays the clay back down round at home, and a new layout lays a fresh body down in the colour it had. On Android below 13 the grain on the paper and in the clay is a fixed fine speckle without the soft mottling, which needs a runtime shader.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [ClayPressBlobDemo.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/playground/claypressblob/ClayPressBlobDemo.kt)

### Files of the block

- [ClayPressBlob.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/playground/claypressblob/ClayPressBlob.kt)
- [ClayPressBlobPhysics.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/playground/claypressblob/ClayPressBlobPhysics.kt)

### Shared helpers the block uses

- [kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt)

### Libraries

It needs no library beyond a new Compose project.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
